items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: I just went there with my cousin Richard.

ctx.x: Well why did you play in the district? I didn't play that much, no, don't forget.

I know you weren't playing. Oh, oh, oh. I tell you I got a beating for that. I mean a good win for that. Yes, indeed. I went and played at the place they used to call Alozo's in New Iberia. I was quite a lad. I was only fifteen years old. And when I came here, somebody went there with my cousin, and somebody told my father that I played in Napoleon's place, he said, where at? They said, Alozo's. What was you doing in Alozo? I said, well I didn't know any better, I just went there with my cousin Richard. And…

those places from that day on. Tell me, did you notice in the people that you associated with sort of an attitude of looking down their nose at you because you were a jazz player, did you meet any of that at all in New Orleans? Well that's good. I'm glad they didn't. I know in North Louisiana, how I was raised in a very strict Protestant atmosphere. All of this was looked upon as being highly sinful and so on, you know.
